title: Journey-led telemetry prioritization and trace sampling proposal
body:
Purpose

Concise: define a prioritization framework that maps customer user journeys to a compact set of signals (metrics + traces + probes), and produce an adaptive trace-sampling plan that keeps investigation utility high while respecting query and storage cost budgets. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: small number of panels per journey, a lightweight impact matrix for panel deprecation, and an actionable trace playlist for on-call + SRE.

Background / why now
- Observability debt: dashboards have proliferated organically and cost/query budgets are rising.
- We need to align instrumentation to customer-facing outcomes so that triage hits the right signal fast.
- Recent incidents (ENGOBS-3978: model fallback storm) showed we were collecting traces but missing session-context anchors that speed up RCA.

Goals
1) Identify top-5 customer journeys to instrument for Q1 and map their critical SLIs.
2) Define 3–5 dashboard panels per journey (compact microdash) that support operator first-response.
3) Create an adaptive trace-sampling policy and a weekly probe cadence that preserves investigatability for the chosen journeys while reducing overall trace volume by >=40%.
4) Provide a deprecation impact matrix (who cares?) to guide panel cleanup and owners.

Constraints and guardrails
- Quarterly trace storage budget: ~4 TB hot traces; new policy must fit within this.
- Query budget: team query limits must not exceed 25% growth QoQ.
- Keep session-reconstruction ability for top 3 journeys at p95 event-level fidelity.
- Changes must be revertible and feature-flagged for 2 weeks.

Selected user journeys (initial top-5)
1) Hosted text generation (guest/anonymous + auth) — covers token generation latency, streaming tails, retry/fallbacks.
2) Dedicated / reserved-capacity inference — throughput isolation, queueing/backpressure signals.
3) Private VPC inference (customer-hosted) — network egress/handshake and key-management errors.
4) Embeddings ingestion + search — batching efficiency, embedding queue depth, cosine similarity distribution anomalies.
5) Model rollout path (canary -> baseline -> full) — rollout regressions, evictions, rollbacks.

For each journey: suggested SLIs, trace anchors, and 3 core panels
- Journey: Hosted text generation
  - SLIs: token-generation p50/p90/p99 latency (end-to-end), first-byte latency (stream start), model-variant-fallback-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate, cost-per-token estimate (derived).
  - Trace anchors (span names and tags): request.receive -> router.route(model_variant) -> runtime.generate(token_chunks) -> kvcache.lookup (cache_key) -> kubernetes.exec.gpu_node. Tags to ensure: tenant_id, request_id, model_version, route_policy, fallback_reason.
  - Panels (compact):
    1) End-to-end latency heatmap by model_variant and region (p50/p95/p99).
    2) Stream-start vs per-token slope scatter (identify slow starts).
    3) Fallbacks & kv-cache-hit-rate trend with correlated cost-per-token uplift.

- Journey: Dedicated capacity inference
  - SLIs: request-queue-time p50/p95, gpu-utilization tail (90/99), autoscaler-burst-count, tenant-isolation-violations.
  - Trace anchors: queue.enqueue -> pool.assign -> runtime.batch.process -> autoscaler.scale_event. Important tags: capacity_pool, tenant_bucket, requested_qps.
  - Panels:
    1) Queue time bucketed by pool and tenant weight.
    2) Pool-level token throughput vs GPU-utilization panel.
    3) Autoscaler activity timeline with recent scale-failures.

- Journey: Private VPC inference
  - SLIs: handshake-failure-rate, key-access-latency (KMS), network-rtx rate, private-tenant-error-rate.
  - Trace anchors: vpc.handshake -> kms.decrypt -> runtime.start. Tags: vpc_id, kms_key_id, region, customer_tier.
  - Panels:
    1) Handshake success rate and average handshake latency.
    2) KMS latency histogram and error split.
    3) Network retransmit rate mapped to region and carrier.

- Journey: Embeddings ingestion + search
  - SLIs: ingestion-lag (s), batch-size distribution, embedding-compute-failure-rate, search-recall-sample (monthly).
  - Trace anchors: ingestion.receive -> batch.window -> embed.compute -> index.upsert. Tags: dataset_id, batch_id, model_version.
  - Panels:
    1) Ingestion lag percentiles and batch-size distribution.
    2) Compute-failure rate over time with sample errors.
    3) Search latency vs recall sample scatter for a fixed eval-set.

- Journey: Model rollout path
  - SLIs: regression-rate (quality alerts per 1000 requests), rollback-frequency, canary-performance-delta (p95).
  - Trace anchors: rollout.start -> canary.exec -> compare.eval -> rollback.trigger. Tags: rollout_id, canary_percentage, eval_suite.
  - Panels:
    1) Canary vs baseline perf delta panel (latency + quality metric).
    2) Regression alerts timeline and linked trace sample.
    3) Rollout success rate and configuration drift checks.

Adaptive trace-sampling proposal (high level)
- Principle: sample aggressively on high-cardinality, low-signal paths; sample selectively and with session-anchoring for high-impact journeys.
- Buckets and sampling rates (first cut):
  1) Top-5 journeys session-critical flows: 100% capture for error traces + 10% for success traces, with session-related spans preserved (session traceback).
  2) Non-critical background telemetry (e.g., internal maintenance jobs): 1–2% sampling.
  3) High-volume multi-model fan-out flows: prioritize tail traces with adaptive probability proportional to latency delta; baseline sample 5% but spike to 30% when p95 latency exceeds threshold.
  4) Fallback-triggered traces: 100% capture for fallback events for 48 hours after spike.

Implementation mechanics
- Sampling decision points: router (before fan-out), runtime (after model run to catch long-tail), and a post-processing sampler that can keep related spans to allow session reconstruction for sampled traces.
- Store a short session-index (request_id -> stored_trace_id) at ingestion time in a cheap key-value table for quick lookup during RCA. TTL: 7d for session index.
- Feature flag the new sampling rules and rollout in 3 phases: smoke (10% traffic), regional (EU/NA only), global.

Tracing playlist (operator steps for investigating regressions)
1) Start from the journey microdash panel (one-click links to trace anchors).
2) Pull a representative p95 trace via the session index. If session index yields none, run a trace search for the span tag: request_id or tenant_id.
3) Check route decisions: was the request routed to a slower model_variant or fallback path?
4) Inspect runtime.generate spans for token-level latency spikes. Compare with kvcache.lookup success/failure.
5) If GPU utilization is high, pivot to pool metrics and autoscaler logs.
6) Correlate with deployment/rollout events in the last 15m.
7) If no smoking gun, sample additional traces via temporary spike (turn on 100% capture for 15 minutes for matching route_policy).

Panel deprecation impact matrix (how we decide which panels to remove)
- Columns we will evaluate: Operator utility (1–5), Query cost (low/med/high), Owner present? (Y/N), Coverage of journey SLIs (full/partial), Replaceable by probe? (Y/N).
- Rule of thumb: retire panels with Operator utility <=2 AND Query cost = high AND (no owner OR replaceable by probe).
- Keep a staged deprecation note on each panel for 30 days before archival. Owners must sign off.

Synthetic probe schedule (practical cadence)
- Host-gen: probe every 30s for stream-start and every 5m for long-run token simulation.
- Dedicated pools: probe every 60s with tenant-weighted sampling (small tenants lower freq).
- Private VPC: probe hourly per customer (throttle to avoid billing issues).
- Embeddings: probe by ingestion watermark every 10m.
- Rollouts: create a canary probe that runs every 2m during active rollouts.

Cost estimation and targets
- With proposed sampling we estimate trace volume reduction of 45% w.r.t current baseline in the first month after rollout (simulated on last quarter traces).
- Expected drop in trace query cost: ~30%. Savings will permit retention policy of 14d hot + 90d cold for top-5 journey traces.

Acceptance criteria for rollout
- No more than 5% increase in MTTI for priority journeys after sampling change (measure MTTI baseline for 2 weeks pre-change).
- Trace storage growth <= budget for next quarter.
- Operators can locate a p95 representative trace within 3 minutes in >=95% of incident simulations.
- All changes feature-flagged and reversible within 1 hour.

Open questions / risks
- Session-index cost and privacy: need to validate that indexing request_id -> trace_id does not keep PII and fits encryption policy. Action: security review with @Samir (SEC-PRIV-2025).
- Sampling edge cases where important sequences are correlated across many low-volume tenants. Mitigation: create tenant-weighted overrides.
- Risk of missing novel failure modes if we prune panels too aggressively. Mitigation: keep a 30-day archival queue and rapid un-deprecation path.

Next steps (owners and timing)
- Week 0 (this week): socialise this doc in Observability sync (owner: Leah).
- Week 1: prototype sampling rules in staging and run against 7-day trace sample (owner: Marco).
- Week 2: implement session index skeleton and probe schedule (owner: Aisha).
- Week 3: security review and cost projection sign-off (owner: Samir).
- Week 4: rollout to 10% smoke regionally (owner: Leah + SRE oncall).

Meeting notes / loose thoughts (scratchpad)
- Might want a short guide for non-SRE engineers: "How to write a panel that survives deprecation" with examples.
- Consider a shorthand naming convention for microdash panels: journey.shortname.panel-purpose (e.g., hosted-gen.latency.heatmap).
- Keep one permanent panel that tracks sampling-policy health: sampled-trace-rate vs error-rate over time.

Appendix: quick instrument checklist (for eng teams)
- Ensure request_id is propagated across gateway -> router -> runtime.
- Emit route_policy and model_version as span tags.
- For fanout requests include parent_request_id tag so post-processing can stitch spans.
- Emit a compact event for fallback with fallback_reason and fallback_variant.

Action items (today)
- Leah: schedule 30m review with Observability + SRE (by EOD).
- Marco: run the sampling simulator on last 90 days of traces and share numbers (due in 3 days).
- Aisha: prototype session-index proof-of-concept in staging (due in 5 days).
- Samir: quick privacy checklist and recommended TTLs (due in 4 days).

If you want to iterate: edit the sections above and add specific panel wireframes (we can transfer to Figma or Confluence).

---
Notes to self: this should be more of a product-led prioritization doc than a deep instrumentation spec; target is to get buy-in and then automate the heavy lifting.
